sections.title: What is Photosynthesis?
sections.body: Have you ever wondered how plants eat? Plants do not eat like animals. They make their own food using sunlight, water, and air. This process is called photosynthesis.

sections.title: How Do Plants Make Food?
sections.body: Plants take water from the soil through their roots. They get carbon dioxide, a gas, from the air through tiny holes in their leaves called stomata. The green part inside leaves, called chlorophyll, catches sunlight. The plant uses sunlight's energy to turn water and carbon dioxide into sugar, which is its food.

sections.title: What Do Plants Give Off?
sections.body: While making food, plants give off oxygen into the air. This oxygen is what people and animals need to breathe. So, plants help us by making food and fresh air!

sections.title: Common Misconceptions About Photosynthesis
sections.body: Some people think plants get their food from the soil, but soil only gives water and minerals. Plants actually make their food in their leaves. Also, plants take in carbon dioxide, not oxygen, during photosynthesis. And only green leaves with chlorophyll can catch sunlight well.

sections.title: Let's Remember
sections.body: Photosynthesis means plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make sugar for food and give off oxygen. Leaves are the main place where this happens. Without sunlight, plants cannot make food and will get weak.

activity.title: Leaf Cover Experiment
materials: A potted plant with green leaves
steps: Cover one leaf of the plant with a small piece of foil.
Leave the plant in sunlight for one week.
Observe and compare the covered leaf with the uncovered leaves.
Ask yourself: What changed? Why do you think this happened?

lesson.notes: The lesson uses a simple experiment and everyday examples like plants we eat to connect learning to daily life.

teacher.teacherOverview: This lesson covers how plants make their own food through photosynthesis, focusing on the roles of sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide, and what plants give off during the process. It also clarifies common misconceptions and identifies the leaf as the main site of photosynthesis. The quiz includes 5 questions to check student understanding. The pack is ready for use.
teachingTips: Prepare the Leaf Cover Experiment materials ahead of time to demonstrate how sunlight affects photosynthesis.
Pre-teach the vocabulary word 'stomata' to help students understand how plants take in carbon dioxide.
Ask students to explain why plants give off oxygen and how this benefits people and animals.
Watch for misconceptions that plants get their food from soil rather than making it in their leaves.
